Key Takeaways

  • Government monthly allowance (2026–2027 cycle): COP$2,484,348 per month (covers about three minimum salaries)
  • One-time support amounts (government cycle): Books COP$401,321 and installation COP$425,400 (one-time payments)
  • Typical living stipend in scholarship programs: Approximately $600 per month in programs that include a living grant
  • Academic eligibility example: Maximum age 50 and a bachelor’s average of 4.0/5.0 required for a recent government cycle
  • Institutional aid scale: Some universities reported average first-year grants of $77,908 and total grants of $240 million

Scholarships in Colombia

Scholarships in Colombia are offered by the government, universities, and private organisations. They can cover full or partial tuition and may include living costs and health insurance. Programs exist for bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral study. Language requirements depend on the program: Spanish for Spanish-taught degrees and TOEFL or IELTS for English-taught programs. Typical awards include a monthly living stipend of about $600 in some programs and, for a recent government cycle, a monthly allowance of COP$2,484,348 plus one-time book and installation payments.

Government Scholarships

What they cover

  • Full tuition in some cycles.
  • Monthly living allowance: COP$2,484,348 in a recent government cycle.
  • One-time book stipend: COP$401,321.
  • One-time installation payment: COP$425,400.
  • Health insurance included in the fully funded cycle.

Common eligibility and rules

  • Open to foreign citizens in some cycles.
  • Maximum age example: 50 for the 2026–2027 government cycle.
  • Academic requirement example: bachelor’s degree with an average of 4.0/5.0.
  • Admission required to a graduate program listed in the national Catalog of Academic Offer.

Key dates and visa notes

  • Application deadline example: June 2026 (to be confirmed).
  • Visa needs: proof of funds, health insurance, and admission to a recognised institution. See the Colombia visa page for details: Colombia visa.

University Scholarships and Institutional Aid

What to expect from universities

  • Some institutions meet 100% of demonstrated financial need for admitted first-year students.
  • Examples of institutional aid scale include average first-year grants near $77,908 and total grants around $240 million across awarded aid pools.
  • International-specific aid pools can be substantial; one reported international aid pool was $19 million for an academic year.

Eligibility and typical requirements

  • Admission offer from the university.
  • Demonstrated financial need for need-based awards.
  • Proof of language proficiency: Spanish for Spanish-taught programs or TOEFL/IELTS for English-taught programs.
  • Academic transcripts and other admission documents.

Private Scholarships and Loan-scholarship Programs

What private funds provide

  • Private programs and foundations can offer tuition support and monthly stipends.
  • Loan-scholarship models can finance postgraduate study and may include partial condonation under specific conditions.

Scale and outcomes

  • Private financing schemes have supported thousands of professionals since the early 1990s.
  • National commitments can channel large sums into private financing until certain dates.
  • Some programs have helped students attend nearly 880 universities abroad.

Eligibility and documentation

  • Requirements vary by provider.
  • Typical needs include admission to a recognised program and proof of language proficiency when required.

How to Prepare a Scholarship Application

Checklist of required documents (based on common requirements)

  • Academic transcripts and degree certificates.
  • Proof of language proficiency (Spanish or TOEFL/IELTS for English programs).
  • Official admission letter or evidence of admission to a recognised institution.
  • Proof of funds for visa purposes where required.
  • Proof of health insurance where required.

Application steps (general)

  1. Confirm which scholarship type fits your profile: government, university, or private.
  2. Check the specific cycle dates and the application deadline.
  3. Secure admission to a recognised program that the funding body accepts.
  4. Assemble transcripts and language test results.
  5. Complete the fund’s application form and submit before the deadline.
  6. Prepare any visa documents once you have an award letter.

Deadlines and cycles

  • Government cycles and embassy-supported funds set deadlines in advance of the academic year.
  • Example cycle to note: some embassy-supported funds listed an academic year of 2025–26 and government funding listed a 2026–2027 cycle.

Search for live opportunities

  • To find current openings that match your level and language, search scholarships on our platform: search scholarships.

Application Advice and Selection Criteria

What selectors commonly check

  • Academic record and transcripts.
  • Proof of language ability for the program language.
  • Alignment of career stage with the award level.
  • Financial need for need-based awards.

One sentence of practical advice

  • Give clear evidence of your academic record and language ability, and match your documents exactly to the funder’s listed requirements to make a strong application.

Frequently asked questions

How much can scholarships in Colombia pay per month?

Some scholarship programs provide a living stipend near $600 per month. A recent fully funded government cycle offered a monthly allowance of COP$2,484,348.

Who is eligible for government scholarships in Colombia?

Eligibility varies by cycle, but an example government cycle allowed foreign citizens, set a maximum age of 50, and required a bachelor’s average of 4.0/5.0 plus admission to a listed graduate program.

Do scholarships cover health insurance?

Some programs include health insurance. A recent fully funded government cycle explicitly covered health insurance for awardees.

What documents do I need to apply?

Common required documents are academic transcripts, proof of language proficiency (Spanish or TOEFL/IELTS), an admission letter to a recognised program, proof of funds for visa needs, and proof of health insurance where required.

When are government scholarship deadlines?

Deadlines differ by cycle. For one government cycle the application deadline was listed as June 2026 (to be confirmed), and embassy-supported programs set deadlines before the academic year start, for example the 2025–26 academic year.
